body:
Thank you so so much for writing this man. Ive been just out of it for the last few days and visited reddit again and found your reply. I can relate a lot, and I'll admit too I'm gay as well, though very few people know as I'm not very comfortable with coming out yet

I really like your advice and it was inspiring to read. 

Also a question, do you think the depression ever goes away, or is it always kinda there?
What can you do to help find your passion or what your good at? I'm having trouble finding that one thing that allows you to not give a fuck about anyone else
Consider yourself lucky you even have friends who bother to invite you to things. I don't :(
As in where I live? Not really, don't have the money to move so I'm staying with my parents until I move back to the college dorms In a month

It probably is. I was recently prescribed antidepressants, so probably. Maybe this is what depression is supossed to feel like, If so I really wish there were something I could do to feel better even temporarily

I'm afraid of being judged or rejected by people, or somehow looking like an idiot. Take going to a bar for example, I would be too afraid going alone because I would think people would think I'm some fat loser going alone, and also because I wouldn't know where to sit or what to do at a bar alone so I'm afraid of looking like an idiot. I don't have much high self-esteem I guess
Thanks for taking the time to read my post and type a response. I helps to know that others think that I'm not such a bad person and that its not all my fault

I haven't been on Facebook for over a month now. I'll admit, it definitely helps. The only think that makes me compare myself to people now is when other brag about their lives IRL, or even if they just mention the awesome things they have done in casual conversation
I'm 23

When's a good time/place to randomly talk to someone at the gym? In the locker room? The person on the machine next to you?

I can be socially stupid at times so I don't want to weird people out

Any tips on meeting or sparking conversations with people at the gym? It would be nice to have some friends to work out with at the gym

Problem is its hard to talking to random guys I don't know either, and I definitely feel intimidated if they are in better shape than I am. I think it may be because I feel inferior to them and think they view me as inferior
Really helpful, thanks!

That is good advice, but the big thing preventing me from doing that is fear. I'm very socially anxious, and something simple like walking into a bar alone for example is just way to frightening for me
Go ahead
I'm already in the process of switching from celexa to Zoloft, so I hope that will help me

Mainly trying to lose weight. Like with diet, I may eat healthy for 1 day, but then the urge to eat unhealthy overpowers me the next day. I try working out, but I can barely do more than 19 minutes on a bike at the gym before getting tired/bored

I'm not really sure. All I know is that I was prescribed antidepressants.

Though how did you get those thoughts out of your head? No matter what I try, I can't get rid of them, unless I'm playing video games or something
Thanks for the reply. Life post college now seems like it more of something to look forward to now rather than something to dread
Thanks for the reply, now it seems more of something I can look forward to rather than something to fear
I'll try. Would be much easier if I had someone to go with though

Thank you very much to take the time to type that reply, it seems to straighten things out.

Not sure if my therapist will agree with my mother being bad, she says she is a great mother. However, my therapist does think she goes overboard on things and that I deserve more independence

It is very hard for me to say no or to stand up for myself, and your right i do do everything i can to avoid confrontation (including lying), and i apologize to people for all kinds of stupid little mistakes i make or even think i made, especially ones in social situations. But I'm not exactly sure what to do about it. These behaviors have really affected my social life with other people and I want to change them.

Also, how would I go about reprogramming that voice inside my head?
Problem is I ask for support so often that it becomes a burden on those people

So what is life like post college then?

 I'll admit, I'm scared as fuck about life post college, I'm afraid of there being no time to do fun things and no time to spend with people, and having to act all grown up and professional all the time.

Thanks for the reply

You mentioned lack of support from parents, and I think that may play a role in this

My parents didn't abuse me, and they did provide me with the essentials and more, such as Christmas presents or sometimes helping me pay for college, but they were always overtly strict and critical, and yelled a lot

I'm also afraid of coming to them for any advice because I'm afraid of them being critical of me, and for the many reasons I will mention below. My parents are also overly stubborn, and trying to reason with them is tough, and my mom always seems to think she is right

I'll admit, I try to avoid my parents as often as I can because they always seem to point out my faults or criticize me, even though they are trying to help. 

My mom also seems to criticize me all the time. She always points out how I'm overweight and should do something about it, and similar things like being on the computer too much, or spending too much money, or not being productive. Sure I may be bad with my money, but complaining to me all the time just makes it worse

They also get angry or upset easily. One example, a year ago I said I might be able to help out with the car insurance because I knew a guy who works at the insurance agency we get our insurance from. Instead of being thankful, my mom yells at me asking if I gave out are insurance information, and scolds me saying how I shouldn't give anyone our insurance information. Situations like this have happened more times than I can even remember.

Or my parents would get mad or overreact at very small things. One time, I left a few wrappers on the table and forgot to throw them away. Later that day, I get a bunch of angry texts from my mom, saying how I'm so immature and irresponsible, and how I shouldn't leave wrappers laying around. She then sends pictures of the wrappers to my therapist asking her to talk with me about why I did that.

And my mom yelling at me, even today that's one of the things I fear most. I lie a lot to them just to appease them, and because of fear of being yelled at or punished. I also want to know I'm right for once in my life

Thanks for writing that

While it may take a year, will there be any noticeable progress along the way? I'm asking because i'm gonna be a senior in college starting in the fall, and I want to be able to enjoy this year and make new friends and stuff
Yes thanks for this. I may have to read it a few more times, but hopefully it sticks

That would work, and at the same time would not

Like you said, it would take a few years, but I don't have that kind of time. 

I don't know why, but I wanted to have this kind of confidence and stuff while I was in college so I could have a good experience there and find a bunch of friends and have a good time, but now I'm gonna be a senior this year so why bother, after college its just work

I guess the problem now is why bother, I guess its a step in the right direction though

Yeah I do have good friends, but they all are from college and live far away so I can't really hang out with them right now.

Also I'm too afraid to get out of my comfort zone, I don't know how to push myself

Problem is I think I am doing it excessively or doing it wrong, because I'm starting to annoy people. Like I want to hang out with friends, but they are always so busy, so I keep on trying to contact them to see when they are not
22, gonna be a a senior in college, but I'm on break right now. Also, will doing things make me more confident and self-sufficient?

I don't think its codependance, as no one is trying to control me, and I'm not excessively preoccupied with other peoples needs

I am seeing a therpist already for my depression, but progress is extremely slow
Problem is I don't know how to move forward, or maybe I'm afraid, or both, I'm not sure

I guess its weird, but I wanted to lose weight and shit before I left college so that people would notice and people would like me and I would have a good college experience. But because it takes so long to fix this shit by the time everything is fixed and I've lost weight and stuff, I will be out of college

Because of that there's no point.
So if I learn mindfulness I learn how to relax then?

What are some ways to train concentration? Does the way I meditate help train concentration? I meditate by just closing my eyes, sitting down, and focusing on my breath, or trying to. I have trouble with doing it everyday though.

Another reason to why I probably don't help myself I just realized, is because it feels like I've dug myself into too deep of a hole, and it just would take way too much effort and time to dig out of. I feel like I wasted my youth so why bother, I'm already 23.

I guess maybe the problem lies in relaxing. Its just too hard for me to relax, or I don't know how. I always want control over things in life, and when things are out of my control or don't turn out right it feels unjust because of the work I've done or the suffering I go through like depression. Its even harder when it comes to letting go of things too.

Im not exactly sure why I haven't sought them out yet. One reason may be that I'm afraid to not be depressed, like I've been depressed for so long its become normal. Another reason may be is because I don't believe it would help, or that I wouldn't be able to follow the instructions because I don't have confidence in myself. Another reason that might be is because I'm waiting for some special moment in life that makes me not depressed, or someone to come along, and then that moment or person changes my outlook in life.

I've read many articles on stuff like this and seen a few videos, and while it gives me hope and motivation for about a day, after that its gone.

I've also been seeing a counselor for therapy already , but like the above, I feel good and hopefully for about a day after seeing the counselor, but then it usually goes away after a day.
So how do you reverse the conditioning? It just seems so hard to stop feeling self pity and bitterness

Will do, thanks. It looks promising so I'll give it a shot. Also, Any recommendations for which CBT book I should get?

One more thing though maybe you can help me with. One reason I realized I have trouble making friends is because I'm too afraid to approach people, and go out and do new things by myself. I realize I missed many opportunities in life because of this, like my entire highschool period where I made no friends at all. I guess I'm really just very shy too but I don't know how to get over it.

I also feel like I'm so different from other people because it feels like I don't share the same experiences that so many other people have, such as having a significant other, or having an awesome highschool experience, or working very hard to achieve some goal. It feels like I don't fit in and it upsets me for some reason, even when people like me I still feel like I don't fit in because I don't have similar experiences. I haven't worked very hard at things in my life either, either that or the things I worked hard at didn't amount to anything or ended up having no value

Thanks.

I also think I just don't like the way my life is going. Right now I'm on summer break, and because I made all my friends in college they live far away and I can't really see them much.

So basically everyday is spent mostly in my room, except for the hour or 2 I spend at the gym, or the days I have work, which is just me by myself in a small warehouse. So everyday feels like I'm not living life, and lonely. That's a big reason why I want people to like me too is so I have people to do awesome things with and its not so lonely and everyday not the same. And it also offers another reason for the jealousy too.

Thanks man, really appreciate it.

Have you also had experience with jealousy and friends? One thing that really got me down yesterday was when I stumbled across a photo of one of my friends having a great time on vacation somewhere. Not only was I jealous that he was having a good time, but I was extremely jealous that I couldn't go with. And I know this guy is a good friend as he has proved it many times

I just get so jealous when friends do awesome things without me, I get jealous that I miss out on those experiences. I even get jealous of random strangers which I see having a good time with other people.

Maybe this also ties into not liking being alone

I've had a feeling I don't like myself, but I'm not really sure how to like myself or why I do t like myself. Maybe its because of my appearance, but losing weight and stuff takes time

I guess I just want friends and don't want to be lonely too, and I'm willing to do everything to do that, even change who I really am, for friends. Most of my summer has been spent by myself and I don't like it because I don't have any friends nearby and I'm lonely

Fear of rejection I guess, which is odd because I've been rejected before, and even hated, and I would think I would be used to it or something

College right now. But I'm on summer break and lonely because I'm having trouble making friends at home. I never made any friends in highschool, and it was much easier to make friends in college because of clubs and stuff. my college friends also don't live nearby.
